CLucene Mobile: binary-package third-party notices
================================================

Scope
-----
This document covers the core/shared binary package and optional highlighter,
not a complete license inventory of every preserved source-repository file.
Do not treat it as a blanket license grant or completed legal clearance.
Keep it with LICENSE-CLucene, the LGPL-2.1 text (LGPL.license, in
Vendor/clucene/upstream of the SwordKit repository), NOTICE, and CHANGES.txt
when distributing the XCFramework. No third-party component is relicensed by this document.

1. CLucene and optional highlighter
----------------------------------
Core CLucene source notices offer the Apache License 2.0 or the GNU Lesser
General Public License. SwordKit uses CLucene under the LGPL, version 2.1, the
option that is compatible with GPL-2.0-only (owner's decision, 2026-11-16); the
Apache option is not selected. The LGPL-2.1 text is LGPL.license in
Vendor/clucene/upstream of the SwordKit repository. The full Apache License,
Version 2.0 is provided in LICENSE-CLucene (LICENSE in the source repository)
for this port's own files and for notices that offer it; it is not the licence
this package is used under. CLucene is linked as static libraries: the
repository holds CLucene as released, the patches and the build, so a modified
CLucene can be built and relinked (LGPL-2.1, section 6).

Copyright (C) 2003-2006 Ben van Klinken and the CLucene Team.
Other authors' copyright notices remain in the source files and headers.

Highlighter source notices include:
Copyright 2002-2004 The Apache Software Foundation.
Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0.
The default build excludes highlighter. Its notices apply if it is enabled.

4. Unicode character data: historical provenance still to verify
---------------------------------------------------------------
File: src/shared/CLucene/config/_gunichartables.h.
This generated table declares G_UNICODE_DATA_VERSION "4.0". Its wrapper source
points to UnicodeData.txt and the Unicode copyright page, but does not contain
the original data license or identify the exact input files used to generate it.

Official investigation starting points:
https://www.unicode.org/Public/4.0-Update/
https://www.unicode.org/Public/4.0-Update/ReadMe-4.0.0.txt
https://www.unicode.org/Public/4.0-Update/UCD-4.0.0.html
https://www.unicode.org/versions/Unicode4.0.0/
https://www.unicode.org/copyright.html
https://www.unicode.org/license.txt

The official 4.0 ReadMe is dated 2003 April 16. It identifies the 4.0.0 data
release. The release-specific UCD documentation is dated 2003-04-18 and
contains the historical UCD Terms of Use reproduced below. Investigate the
original CLucene/GLib source distribution and table generator to confirm the
exact data inputs. Archived 2003-era Unicode copyright pages and confirmation
from Unicode, Inc. are additional sources if that provenance remains unclear.

Source attribution: Unicode Character Database, Version 4.0.0, Unicode, Inc.
The bundled tables declare version 4.0 and are presented as derived Unicode
character data. This attribution does not claim an exact generator/input match
has been independently verified.

Historical Unicode 4.0 UCD Terms of Use
Retrieved 2026-10-12 from:
https://www.unicode.org/Public/4.0-Update/UCD-4.0.0.html

Disclaimer

The Unicode Character Database is provided as is by Unicode, Inc. No claims are
made as to fitness for any particular purpose. No warranties of any kind are
expressed or implied. The recipient agrees to determine applicability of
information provided. If this file has been purchased on magnetic or optical
media from Unicode, Inc., the sole remedy for any claim will be exchange of
defective media within 90 days of receipt.

This disclaimer is applicable for all other data files accompanying the Unicode
Character Database, some of which have been compiled by the Unicode Consortium,
and some of which have been supplied by other sources.

Limitations on Rights to Redistribute This Data

Recipient is granted the right to make copies in any form for internal
distribution and to freely use the information supplied in the creation of
products supporting the UnicodeTM Standard. The files in the Unicode Character
Database can be redistributed to third parties or other organizations (whether
for profit or not) as long as this notice and the disclaimer notice are retained.
Information can be extracted from these files and used in documentation or
programs, as long as there is an accompanying notice indicating the source.

The file Unihan.txt contains older and inconsistent Terms of Use. That language
is overridden by these terms.

Unicode's current official terms say Data Files and Software are subject to
Unicode License v3 unless a specific release restriction or license says
otherwise. The current license is reproduced below as an additional reference,
not as a replacement for the historical release-specific terms above.
Its inclusion does NOT establish that this old generated table has been traced
to the official data. Verify the derivation before treating this package as
cleared for publication.

5. External dependencies and excluded contributors
--------------------------------------------------
SDK libc++ and zlib implementations are not embedded by this static-library
packaging process. The consuming application's linkage and redistribution
determine any additional runtime notice requirements.

Contributor analysis, Snowball, and contributor streams are not included by
the current build. Snowball's upstream engine has separate BSD-3-Clause terms;
its wrapper has CLucene notices. The contributor PorterStemmer's permission
grant remains unresolved. Those source-repository obligations are not satisfied
by this binary-package document and must be handled before source publication.
